schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Meshy text-to-3D models: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v2/text-to-3d/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v2/text-to-3d` answers with a `MeshyTextTo3DCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle. The family's three other operations (image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d and retexture) stay reachable on their own `/proxy/meshy/...` routes and answer closely related task documents; a `{provider}/{model}` call settles onto the text-to-3d generation, which is the one this schema describes.
The generated mesh is in `model_urls`, at whichever of `glb`, `fbx`, `usdz` and `obj` the request produced — which of them are populated depends on the request, so read the one that is present rather than keying completion off `glb` alone. `glb` is the rendition a `{"mode": "preview"}` task with no format selector answers with, but it is not the only shape a success can take. Two neighbouring fields are NOT interchangeable with a mesh and a caller must not key completion off either: `mtl` is a material sidecar for `obj` rather than a mesh in its own right, and `thumbnail_url` is a preview image rather than the asset the call generated. Comfy Router draws exactly that line — a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying none of those four mesh URLs is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document — so through Router a `200` here always carries a mesh, but not always the same one.
`status` is Meshy's own UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` — forwarded unchanged and not case-folded. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` and `CANCELED` are terminal failures and reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this document, with the provider's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100 and is 100 on a succeeded task.
`type` says which of the operation's two stages produced the document. `text-to-3d-preview` is the geometry stage, requested with `{"mode": "preview"}` and a prompt. `text-to-3d-refine` is the separate, dearer texturing task, requested with `{"mode": "refine"}` against a finished preview's `id` as `preview_task_id`; it is what populates `texture_urls`.
`negative_prompt` and `texture_richness` are fields Meshy keeps for backward compatibility and does not populate meaningfully; `video_url` is likewise deprecated.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Meshy text-to-3D models: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v2/text-to-3d/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v2/text-to-3d` answers with a `MeshyTextTo3DCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle. The family's three other operations (image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d and retexture) stay reachable on their own `/proxy/meshy/...` routes and answer closely related task documents; a `{provider}/{model}` call settles onto the text-to-3d generation, which is the one this schema describes.
The generated mesh is in `model_urls`, at whichever of `glb`, `fbx`, `usdz` and `obj` the request produced — which of them are populated depends on the request, so read the one that is present rather than keying completion off `glb` alone. `glb` is the rendition a `{"mode": "preview"}` task with no format selector answers with, but it is not the only shape a success can take. Two neighbouring fields are NOT interchangeable with a mesh and a caller must not key completion off either: `mtl` is a material sidecar for `obj` rather than a mesh in its own right, and `thumbnail_url` is a preview image rather than the asset the call generated. Comfy Router draws exactly that line — a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying none of those four mesh URLs is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document — so through Router a `200` here always carries a mesh, but not always the same one.
`status` is Meshy's own UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` — forwarded unchanged and not case-folded. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` and `CANCELED` are terminal failures and reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this document, with the provider's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100 and is 100 on a succeeded task.
`type` says which of the operation's two stages produced the document. `text-to-3d-preview` is the geometry stage, requested with `{"mode": "preview"}` and a prompt. `text-to-3d-refine` is the separate, dearer texturing task, requested with `{"mode": "refine"}` against a finished preview's `id` as `preview_task_id`; it is what populates `texture_urls`.
`negative_prompt` and `texture_richness` are fields Meshy keeps for backward compatibility and does not populate meaningfully; `video_url` is likewise deprecated.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Meshy's remesh operation: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/remesh/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/remesh` answers a `MeshyRemeshCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id and which carries no mesh, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle.
`meshy/remesh` names an OPERATION rather than a model version. It re-meshes a mesh the caller already has (identified in the request by a preceding task's id or by a model URL), so it consumes a 3D asset and produces a 3D asset; it is not one of the text-to-3D generations `meshy/meshy-5`, `meshy/meshy-6` and `meshy/meshy-7` name.
The remeshed model is in `model_urls`, at whichever of `glb`, `fbx`, `obj`, `usdz`, `blend` and `stl` the request's `target_formats` asked for — which of them are populated depends on the request, so read the one that is present rather than keying completion off `glb` alone. Comfy Router draws that line: a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying no mesh URL at all is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document, so through Router a `200` here always carries a mesh — but not always the same one. The line is drawn by `classifyMeshy`, which is shared with the text-to-3D family and accepts a seventh leaf, `model_urls.pre_remeshed_glb`, that this operation's `MeshyRemeshModelUrls` does not declare; a task carrying only that key would be forwarded rather than refused.
`status` is Meshy's own UPPERCASE vocabulary, forwarded unchanged and not case-folded. This operation's enum is `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` — note `PROCESSING` where the text-to-3D family says `IN_PROGRESS`, and no `CANCELED`. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` is a terminal failure and reaches a Router caller as a Comfy Router error with Meshy's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100 and is 100 on a succeeded task. `preceding_tasks` is only meaningful while `PENDING`, which a Router caller never sees.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Meshy's rigging operation: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/rigging/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/rigging` answers a `MeshyRiggingCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id and which carries no asset, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle.
`meshy/rigging` names an OPERATION rather than a model version: it adds a skeleton to a mesh the caller already has (a preceding task's id or a model URL), so it consumes a 3D asset and produces one. It is not one of the text-to-3D generations.
The output is under `result`, and this operation shares NO output key with the other Meshy operations. `result.rigged_character_glb_url` and `result.rigged_character_fbx_url` are the rigged character itself. `result.basic_animations` carries six further URLs — a walking and a running clip, each as a skinned GLB, a skinned FBX and an armature GLB. Which of the eight are populated depends on the request, so read the one that is present. Comfy Router draws that line: a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying none of those eight URLs is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document. Note that `result.basic_animations` being present is NOT itself evidence of output — an empty object is representable and carries nothing loadable.
`status` is the shared Meshy UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` — forwarded unchanged. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` and `CANCELED` reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error with Meshy's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100. `expires_at` is when Meshy stops serving the result URLs, so fetch them rather than storing the document.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for every Moonvalley route slug: the terminal `GET /proxy/moonvalley/prompts/{prompt_id}` prompt document, forwarded unchanged. All five operations are SUBMIT-AND-POLL against that ONE status route — the submit answers a prompt handle and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished prompt document rather than that handle.
The generated asset is at `output_url`, whatever the operation's medium: it is an image for `moonvalley/text-to-image` and a video for the other four. Comfy Router draws that line itself — a `completed` prompt carrying no `output_url` is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document — so through Router a `200` here always carries an asset URL. Fetch it; nothing is inlined in this body.
`status` is Moonvalley's own lowercase vocabulary. `completed` is the one terminal success. `error` is a terminal failure and reaches a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this document, with the provider's own detail under `error`. `queued` and `generating` are the in-flight states Router polls through and a caller never sees.
`inference_params`, `model_params`, `meta`, `frame_conditioning` and `error` are free-form objects Moonvalley does not document a shape for; they are forwarded as-is and this schema does not narrow them.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

TextResponseFormatConfiguration.description:
An object specifying the format that the model must output.

Configuring `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables Structured Outputs,
which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the
[Structured Outputs guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the OpenAI Responses text models: the `OpenAIResponse` document `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses` answers with, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` classifies `{provider: openai, endpoint: /v1/responses}` as ReturnModeDirect with no poll route — so the body a caller receives is this finished document from the one call, not a task handle Router polls on.
The generated text is at `output[].content[].text`. Neither container above it is the result on its own: `output` is an array of `OutputItem`, which is a `oneOf` over six item types (`OutputMessage`, the four tool calls, and `ReasoningItem`), so a response whose only items are a `ReasoningItem` or a `web_search_call` carries an `output` that is non-empty and no text at all. Only the `OutputMessage` branch has `content`, and only its `output_text` content part (`OutputTextContent`) has `text` — which is why the nightly SDK case for this family asserts the leaf path `output[].content[].text` rather than the `output` container (`testing/e2e/router_sdk/cases.d/openai_responses.json`). `output_text` at the root is the same text aggregated, but it is an SDK-only convenience field rather than something every client sees, so it is not the leaf to key off.
`status` is OpenAI's own vocabulary (`completed`, `failed`, `in_progress`, `cancelled`, `queued`, `incomplete`), forwarded unchanged. An `incomplete` response still carries whatever text was produced before the cut, with the reason at `incomplete_details.reason` — `max_output_tokens` is the expected one for a request that caps the budget. `error` is populated instead when `status` is `failed`, and `usage` reports OpenAI's own token accounting — OpenAI's numbers, not the Comfy charge.
`stream` and `background` are SETTLED TO FALSE, not merely discouraged. Router CAPTURES a /proxy/ response rather than streaming it and answers a direct-return operation out of that one response, so neither a live stream nor a queued handle can be served here: a streamed request would be answered a document that is not this one AND would go unmetered (the Rewrite's ModifyResponse cannot decode an SSE payload), and `background: true` returns a queued 200 carrying no token counts that the same ModifyResponse would meter off usage the document does not have. Both are therefore forced to `false` on a Router-dispatched request — `routerSettledBoolFields` (`server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go`), the same treatment the Anthropic messages and Gemini Interactions routes already get — so a caller who names either one is answered the document below rather than refused. Both stay fully reachable at `POST /proxy/openai/v1/responses`, which the settlement does not touch.
`model` on the RESULT is the RESOLVED provider-side snapshot OpenAI actually ran (`gpt-4.1` in, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` back), which is a different vocabulary from the request's allowlist — see the note on `ResponseProperties` for why the allowlist enum constrains only the request half.

instructions.description:
Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

When using along with `previous_response_id`, the instructions from a previous
response will not be carried over to the next response. This makes it simple
to swap out system (or developer) messages in new responses.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated for a response, including visible output tokens and [reasoning tokens](/docs/guides/reasoning).

previous_response_id.description:
The unique ID of the previous response to the model. Use this to
create multi-turn conversations. Learn more about
[conversation state](/docs/guides/conversation-state).

verbosity.description: Constrains the verbosity of the model's response. One of `low`, `medium`, or `high`.

tool_choice.description:
How the model should select which tool (or tools) to use when generating
a response. See the `tools` parameter to see how to specify which tools
the model can call.

truncation.description:
The truncation strategy to use for the model response.
- `auto`: If the context of this response and previous ones exceeds
  the model's context window size, the model will truncate the
  response to fit the context window by dropping input items in the
  middle of the conversation.
- `disabled` (default): If a model response will exceed the context window
  size for a model, the request will fail with a 400 error.

TextResponseFormatConfiguration.description:
An object specifying the format that the model must output.

Configuring `{ "type": "json_schema" }` enables Structured Outputs,
which ensures the model will match your supplied JSON schema. Learn more in the
[Structured Outputs guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

The default format is `{ "type": "text" }` with no additional options.

**Not recommended for gpt-4o and newer models:**

Setting to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON mode, which
ensures the message the model generates is valid JSON. Using `json_schema`
is preferred for models that support it.

Learn more about [Structured Outputs](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined
in the `schema` field. Only a subset of JSON Schema is supported when
`strict` is `true`. To learn more, read the [Structured Outputs
guide](/docs/guides/structured-outputs).

type.description: The type of response format being defined. Always `json_schema`.

inputSchema.description:
The request body Comfy Router accepts for the seventeen OpenAI Responses chat and reasoning models, and the schema `routervalidate.Guard` validates a `POST /v2/models/openai/{model}` call against before it reaches OpenAI.
It describes the SHAPE of a Responses request -- which fields exist and what JSON type each carries -- and deliberately does not restate OpenAI's own sub-vocabularies for `input` items, `tools` or `include`. Router forwards the body unchanged, OpenAI extends those vocabularies continuously, and a schema that enumerated them would refuse calls that run today. OpenAI's Responses API reference is authoritative for the contents of those fields; this schema is authoritative for what Router itself will accept.
Fields not listed here are forwarded to OpenAI untouched. Two of them are SETTLED to `false` on the Router surface when a caller names them -- `stream` and `background` -- because Router captures the provider response rather than streaming it, and a streamed or queued document is one this route can neither return nor meter (routerSettledBoolFields, server/middleware/router_model_catalog.go).

example.input: Reply with the single word: ok

input.description: Text, image or file inputs to the model, used to generate a response. The one field of this contract Router cannot supply, and the only entry in `required` below.

oneOf.description: A text input to the model, equivalent to a text input with the `user` role.
oneOf.title: Text input

oneOf.description: A list of one or many input items. See OpenAI's Responses API reference for the item taxonomy; Router does not narrow it.
oneOf.title: Input item list

instructions.description: Inserts a system (or developer) message as the first item in the model's context.

max_output_tokens.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens generated for a response, including visible output tokens and reasoning tokens. On a reasoning id this ceiling is shared with the hidden reasoning tokens, so a small value can consume the whole budget before any visible text -- which is why the reasoning smoke cases send 1024 where the chat ones send 16.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to allow the model to run tool calls in parallel.

previous_response_id.description: The ID of a previous response, for multi-turn conversations.

reasoning.description: REASONING TIER ONLY. Configuration for reasoning models, e.g. `{"effort": "medium"}`. Forwarded unchanged; see OpenAI's reasoning guide for the accepted keys. A chat-tier id ignores it.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. CHAT TIER ONLY: the o-series reasoning ids (`o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) reject this parameter at OpenAI. Router does not refuse it for them -- see this component's note on why the two tiers share one schema -- so a reasoning call that sends it is answered by OpenAI's own error.

text.description: Output-format configuration, e.g. `{"format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` for Structured Outputs. Forwarded unchanged.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select which tool to use. Either a string mode or an object naming a tool.

tools.description: Tool definitions the model may call. Router does not narrow the tool taxonomy; see OpenAI's Responses API reference for the accepted shapes.

top_p.description: Nucleus-sampling cutoff. CHAT TIER ONLY, on the same terms as `temperature`.

truncation.description: Truncation strategy when the context exceeds the model's window. The enum IS enforced here, unlike the three vocabularies above, because these two values are the complete set OpenAI documents and it has not grown. An explicit `null` is still accepted, on the same terms as the fields above it.
